result:
Two findings, handled differently.

**Minor (typo):** a real defect, so I fix it. It is a docstring-only change with no behavior to put under a RED test, so I record that in the ledger instead.

<edit path="rates/card.py">
    '''Round a price to whole cents. A tie goes to the nearest even cent.'''
</edit>

<command>
make test > .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log 2>&1; tail -n 15 .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log
</command>

<command>
git add rates/card.py && git commit -m "fix: correct typo in round_price docstring" && printf '%s\n' "Final review fix: typo 'neerest' -> 'nearest' in round_price() docstring (docstring-only, no RED test possible; make test green)" "Ruling: Did NOT switch round_price() to ROUND_HALF_UP (review finding, Important) — plan Decision D2 (owner, 2026-11-02) mandates ROUND_HALF_EVEN to match the ledger system; the reviewer's \"customers expect half-up\" is an unsourced claim that contradicts a binding owner decision, and the plan's tests encode half-even — if wrong, ties (x.xx5) round one cent low versus customer expectation and the ledger-matching guarantee is kept; reversing is a one-line change plus test updates once the owner revises D2" >> .sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md
</command>

**Why I declined the Important finding:** D2 is an explicit owner decision recorded in the plan, and the spec and plan are the binding authority. The reviewer did not have that context and gave no evidence for the half-up claim. Changing the rounding would silently break the match with the ledger system. This is a ruling rather than one of the five stops. Nothing is irreversible, and the code stays as the owner specified. I leave the product question with the owner.

Next I follow the plan-completion protocol in `references/final-review.md`. I do not delete the workspace yet, because `progress.md` holds the ruling you need to see at the gate.

**Message to my partner:**

> Plan 14 (rate card) is complete. All tasks are in the ledger, `make test` passes, and the whole-branch review is done.
>
> **Fixed:** a typo in the `round_price()` docstring ("neerest" → "nearest"). It is committed, and `make test` is still green.
>
> **Not changed, needs your attention:** the reviewer asked to switch `round_price()` from ROUND_HALF_EVEN to ROUND_HALF_UP because "customers expect half-up." I did not do this. Decision D2 (owner, plan review, 2026-11-02) requires half-even to match the ledger system, and the reviewer cited no evidence for the customer claim. The ruling is in `.sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md`.
>
> If customer-facing prices really should be half-up, that conflicts with D2 and the owner should decide. It would also create a rounding mismatch with the ledger. The change itself is small: swap the constant in `rates/card.py` and update the tie-case tests.
>
> The `.sdd/14-rate-card/` workspace is still in place so you can read the ledger. Tell me when to run `finishing-a-development-branch`.
